title: introduce-cost-trace-analyzer-and-prefill-policy-simulator
author: Aisha Gupta
release_notes: Add Cost Trace Analyzer and Prefill Policy Simulator: new telemetry tags, a dry-run simulator CLI to estimate unit-econ impact of prefill/batching/quant defaults, and recommendations output. No breaking changes to public API. Includes opt-in flag for private deployments.

b9d4c3a: implement probabilistic cache model and cost-matrix exporter

description:
Motivation: we frequently get requests to understand the unit-econ impact of prefill and cache defaults without risking production changes. Operators need a way to dry-run policy changes (batch size, prefill fraction, quant tier) against representative traffic and produce an easy-to-interpret cost delta matrix and conservative recommendation for rollout.

What this PR introduces: 1) Cost Trace Analyzer: a standalone CLI tool (tools/cost-trace-analyzer) that consumes sampled request traces (ndjson) and produces a CSV/JSON cost-matrix outlining token-level cost, expected latency percentiles, and cache hit statistics per tested policy. 2) Prefill Policy Simulator: runtime-side component (services/runtime/src/prefill/policy_simulator.go) that can be invoked in dry-run mode via the console or as part of a canary pipeline. The simulator uses a probabilistic KV-cache model (configurable TTL, size cap, and eviction distribution) combined with batching heuristics to estimate both cost and latency SLO impact. 3) Telemetry: new tags (telemetry/tags.go) emitted when running dry-run analysis or when running in staged mirroring; fields include cost_trace_id, prefill_decision, quant_suggestion, sampled_tenant_id. 4) Recommendations engine: a lightweight rule-based scorer that ranks tested policies by conservative unit-cost reduction while honoring latency SLO budgets; outputs top-3 candidate policies and a safety score. 5) CLI and docs: docs/ops/prefill-simulator.md documents how to run the analyzer and interpret the cost matrix; ci/perf/smoke-prefill.yml adds a smoke run to CI that exercises the analyzer on a small synthetic trace.

Implementation notes: - Probabilistic cache model: we model prefix reuse by hashing request prefixes into a slot map and simulating a TTL with an exponential decay; eviction is approximated by a capped LRU probabilistic sampler to keep sim cost low. - Batching approximation: we replay sequence lengths and simulate windowed batching with an adjustable max-batch and microbatch toggles; token production cost is computed using current model catalog pricing + quant tier multipliers. - Quant suggestion: we run policies against 3 quant tiers (full, q4/8, q8/16 equivalents) and estimate quality loss via a heuristic signal (length-normalized perplexity proxy derived from token-level logits saved in sampled traces). This is conservative and flagged as an advisory only. - Privacy: all trace ingestion is opt-in; CLI supports a scrub step that removes user identifiers before analysis. - Performance: analyzer processes ~250K requests / minute in single-threaded mode on a m5.large equivalent; designed for short diagnostic runs.

Testing & results: - Integration tests added (tests/integration/prefill_simulator_test.go) with synthetic traces covering cold-start, burst, and long-tail patterns. - CI perf smoke runs use a 5K-request synthetic trace and validate that the cost matrix generation completes under 90s. - In an internal demo using an e-commerce workload trace, the top recommendation produced by the simulator reduced expected per-call token-cost by ~12% while keeping 95th P99 latency within the configured SLO (200ms).

Migration and rollout: - Feature is opt-in. Prefill simulator is behind the runtime flag enable_prefill_dry_run; telemetry tags require enable_cost_trace_tagging. - Docs include a step-by-step: run analyzer locally -> validate recommendations in staging via traffic mirroring -> schedule canary rollout with capped percent.

Checklist: - [x] Implement analyzer + CLI - [x] Integrate simulator with runtime prefill hooks - [x] Add telemetry fields and schema doc - [x] Add integration tests and CI smoke - [x] Add docs and example runbook - [x] Security review: scrub option implemented

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: quant suggestions may under-estimate quality regressions. Mitigation: suggestions are advisory; we tag recommendations with a conservatism score and require manual evals before rollout. - Risk: simulator divergence from live cache dynamics. Mitigation: we compare simulator outputs to sampled staging traces and include a delta report; major mismatches surface as a safety signal in recommendations.

How to try it: 1) pip install (sdk/python/redwood/cost_tooling.py) or use the binary at tools/cost-trace-analyzer/cli ; 2) run: ./cost-trace-analyzer --trace sample.ndjson --policies policies.json --output report.json ; 3) follow docs/ops/prefill-simulator.md for interpreting results.

Related: ENG-2481 (prefill dry-run), ENG-2503 (telemetry standardization), SUP-7123 (customer ask: conservative quant rollouts).
smoke_test_result: passed after one rerun (first run flaky due to network timeout against external sample store).
